title: Differential basis quotient has vanishing localized cotangent obstructions
statement: Let R,D,Q be commutative rings, D a smooth R-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], and Q an R-algebra whose structure map R→Q is surjective. Let σ:D→Q be an R-algebra homomorphism, n≥0, and f:Fin n→D with σ(fᵢ)=0. Suppose 1⊗dfᵢ is a Q-basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module] of Q⊗_D Ω[D/R] [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], using σ for the D-action. Set a=(fᵢ) and C=D/a. Given a ring homomorphism τ:C→Q with τ∘(D→C)=σ, every prime q of C containing ker τ has H₁(L[C/R])_q=0 and Ω[C/R]_q=0 (the localizations of modules [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]).

source.place: Tag 07M7, second paragraph, the Jacobi-Zariski sequence and rank/Nakayama argument through H₁ and Ω vanishing

proof.text: Set C=D/(fᵢ). Smoothness gives projectivity of Ω[D/R] and vanishing of H₁(L[D/R]). Apply the smooth Jacobi-Zariski quotient sequence to a=(fᵢ). The map δ:a/a²→C⊗_D Ω[D/R] sends the class of fᵢ to 1⊗dfᵢ; its kernel identifies with H₁(L[C/R]) and its cokernel with Ω[C/R].

Fix q⊇ker τ and pull back to p in D. The identity τ∘mk=σ implies ker σ⊆p. Surjectivity of R→Q implies σ is surjective, so D/ker σ≅Q and the map D→κ(p) factors through Q. The given basis specializes to a κ(p)-basis of Ω[D/R]⊗_D κ(p) of size n. The finite projective module Ω[D/R]_p is free and its rank is this residue-field dimension, hence n. Therefore (C⊗_D Ω[D/R])_q is free of rank n over C_q.

Modulo the maximal ideal of C_q the images δ(fᵢ) form the given residue-field basis. Nakayama implies δ_q is surjective. Since the fᵢ generate a, their conormal classes generate (a/a²)_q, giving a surjection ψ:C_q^n→(a/a²)_q. Choose a basis identification θ of the target of δ_q with C_q^n. The composite θδ_qψ is a surjective endomorphism of a finite module, hence bijective. Injectivity of the composite implies injectivity of ψ; its surjectivity makes ψ bijective. For any element killed by δ_q, lift it along ψ and use injectivity of the composite to see it is zero. Thus δ_q is bijective.

Localization preserves exactness of the Jacobi-Zariski sequence. The localized H₁ injects into ker δ_q=0, and the localized Ω is the cokernel of the surjective δ_q, hence zero. Zero additive modules are subsingleton, giving both conclusions.

theorem localized_cotangent_vanishes_of_section_differential_basis
    (R D Q : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing D] [CommRing Q]
    [Algebra R D] [Algebra R Q] [Smooth R D]
    (σ : D →ₐ[R] Q) (hπ : Function.Surjective (algebraMap R Q))
    (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → D) (hf : ∀ i, σ (f i) = 0)
    (hb : letI : Algebra D Q := σ.toRingHom.toAlgebra
      ∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin n) Q (Q ⊗[D] KaehlerDifferential R D),
        ∀ i, b i = 1 ⊗ₜ[D] KaehlerDifferential.D R D (f i))
    (τ : (D ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f)) →+* Q)
    (hτ : τ.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range f))) = σ.toRingHom) :
    ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum (D ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f)),
      RingHom.ker τ ≤ q.asIdeal →
        Subsingleton (LocalizedModule q.asIdeal.primeCompl
          (H1Cotangent R (D ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f)))) ∧
        Subsingleton (LocalizedModule q.asIdeal.primeCompl
          (KaehlerDifferential R (D ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f))))
